summary: The statement and proof are correct. Attempts to refute the claim using an empty parity class, singleton support, rank-zero sublevels, identically zero cost, zero minimum shifted cost, and coincident cutoff costs reveal no failure. The maximum defining M is attained at a finite support cost. Each of the three counting bounds follows from an injective lattice map or the verified finite-sumset inequality, with the actual affine rank and the rank-zero case handled correctly. The subgroup construction gives exactly the required 2^r residue-class bound without a full-rank assumption. The layer identities, selected-level estimates, integrations, and constants 12, 4, and 6 are valid, including all closed-cutoff boundaries. Summation over parity classes and the supremum over all real shifts give the stated consequence. The publisher's abstract at https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01302969 confirms the quoted Ruzsa inequality, and its hypotheses hold for the full-dimensional images of B and -B in their real span.
